title: PrivDPR: Synthetic Graph Publishing with Deep PageRank under Differential Privacy

problem.claim: Privacy-preserving synthetic graph publishing must protect individuals' privacy while retaining the utility of the original data.

gap.claim: Existing approaches face high sensitivity from intricate node relationships and premature convergence caused by privacy-budget splitting under small privacy budgets.

contributions.claim: PrivDPR is a privacy-preserving deep PageRank approach for graph synthesis that adds noise to the gradient of a specific weight during learning.
The method uses weight normalization to relate increased layer depth to mitigation of high sensitivity and privacy-budget splitting.
The authors formally analyze PrivDPR and state that its generated synthetic graph satisfies node-level differential privacy.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe PrivDPR as a novel privacy-preserving deep PageRank method for graph synthesis.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world graph datasets show high data utility across multiple graph structural properties.

narrative_sequence.summary: The work targets privacy-preserving synthetic graph publishing that retains data utility.
Prior methods leave sensitivity and small-budget convergence problems unresolved.
The paper introduces PrivDPR, using PageRank-inspired deep graph synthesis with gradient noise.
Weight normalization and increased depth are presented as mechanisms for addressing sensitivity and privacy-budget splitting, with a node-level DP guarantee.
Experiments on real-world graph datasets report high utility across multiple structural properties.

source_observation.claim: The method adds noise to the gradient for a specific weight and uses weight normalization as a bridge to analyze deeper models.

interpretation.claim: Constraining or normalizing parameter effects may help manage sensitivity and privacy-budget allocation in layered graph synthesis.

application.claim: When designing private graph generators, consider localized gradient perturbation together with weight normalization and depth as jointly analyzed controls.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when this strategy fails or how its behavior varies across graph types, privacy budgets, or utility measures.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, structural properties, privacy parameters, baselines, or quantitative utility results.
The abstract does not provide the formal conditions or proof details for the node-level differential privacy guarantee.
